components.note: 鹿 (deer) — a picture of a deer with antlers and legs, as in 麒麟. Appears in 丽 and 麋 too.

example.hanzi: 森林里有一只小鹿。
example.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ yǒu yì zhī xiǎo lù.
example.english: There is a fawn in the forest.
example.fact: 鹿 appears in the idiom 指鹿为马 ('point at a deer and call it a horse'), meaning to deliberately twist the truth. 中原逐鹿 'the deer hunt on the Central Plain' means a contest for power. Its homophone 禄 means official salary.

examples.hanzi: 公园里有一群梅花鹿。
examples.pinyin: Gōngyuán li yǒu yì qún méihuālù.
examples.english: There is a herd of sika deer in the park.

examples.hanzi: 小鹿在草地上奔跑。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎolù zài cǎodì shang bēnpǎo.
examples.english: The fawn runs across the grass.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and swimming, as in 河, 海, 泳: swimming and drifting.
斿 (yóu) gives the exact sound: a flag with streamers that floats freely.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 数千名市民走上街头游行，要求改善环境保护政策。
example.pinyin: shùqiān míng shìmín zǒushàng jiētóu yóuxíng, yāoqiú gǎishàn huánjìng bǎohù zhèngcè.
example.english: Thousands of citizens marched through the streets, demanding improved environmental policies.
example.fact: The 1963 March on Washington drew an estimated 250,000 people and is where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his 'I Have a Dream' speech. Historians widely credit the demonstration with helping build the political momentum that led to the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

examples.hanzi: 节日那天，街上有盛大的游行。
examples.pinyin: Jiérì nà tiān, jiē shàng yǒu shèngdà de yóuxíng.
examples.english: On the festival day there was a grand parade in the street.

examples.hanzi: 学生们举着标语在广场上游行。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshengmen jǔzhe biāoyǔ zài guǎngchǎng shàng yóuxíng.
examples.english: The students marched in the square holding banners.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 胡 first meant the flesh hanging under the chin.
古 (gǔ) — near sound — 胡 is hú; 古 also sounds out 湖 hú and 糊 hú.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
八 (eight) — originally two strokes pulling apart, meaning divide; that sense is in 分 divide, 公 public and 半 half.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 别听他的，那些话完全是胡说八道。
example.pinyin: bié tīng tā de, nàxiē huà wánquán shì húshuōbādào.
example.english: Don't listen to him, that's complete nonsense.
example.fact: A 2018 MIT study published in Science analyzed millions of tweets and found that false stories spread about six times faster than true ones. Researchers attributed this to novelty: surprising claims trigger more sharing than accurate but ordinary information.

examples.hanzi: 你不要胡说八道，这样会误导别人。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ búyào húshuōbādào, zhèyàng huì wùdǎo biéren.
examples.english: Don't talk rubbish; it will mislead others.

examples.hanzi: 他喝醉了，开始胡说八道。
examples.pinyin: Tā hēzuì le, kāishǐ húshuōbādào.
examples.english: He got drunk and started talking nonsense.

components.note: 彡 (patterns, hairlines) — marks shape, shadow and decoration, as in 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 形 is a shape.
开 (a worn-down 幵) hints at the sound: 形 xíng sounds like 刑 and 型.
弋 (yì) is a loose sound clue for shì; 弋 also in 试 shì and 拭 shì.
工 (work, craft) — a craftsman's pattern, a standard.

example.hanzi: 这份报告的形式很正式，但内容有点空洞。
example.pinyin: zhè fèn bàogào de xíngshì hěn zhèngshì, dàn nèiróng yǒudiǎn kōngdòng.
example.english: This report's format is very formal, but the content is a bit empty.
example.fact: Snowflakes almost always grow with six-fold symmetry because water molecules bond into a hexagonal lattice as ice crystallizes. Yet no two snowflakes have ever been proven identical, since tiny shifts in humidity and temperature during formation shape each one in a slightly different way.

examples.hanzi: 这次会议只是走形式，没有实际意义。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì huìyì zhǐshì zǒu xíngshì, méiyǒu shíjì yìyì.
examples.english: This meeting is just a formality and has no real meaning.

examples.hanzi: 这个活动以比赛的形式进行。
examples.pinyin: Zhège huódòng yǐ bǐsài de xíngshì jìnxíng.
examples.english: This activity is held in the form of a contest.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫; 嘴 is a mouth or lips.
觜 (zuǐ) — same sound — 嘴 is zuǐ, like 觜.
口 (mouth) — marks the mouth and speech, as in 吃, 喝, 吹; 唇 is the lip.
辰 (chén) hints at the sound: 唇 chún is close to 晨 chén and 振 zhèn.

example.hanzi: 冬天风大，她的嘴唇都干裂了。
example.pinyin: dōngtiān fēng dà, tā de zuǐchún dōu gānliè le.
example.english: The wind was strong in winter, and her lips became chapped.
example.fact: Human lips have no sweat glands or oil glands, and the skin covering them is far thinner than skin elsewhere on the face. This leaves blood vessels closer to the surface, which is why lips look redder than surrounding skin and dry out so much faster in cold or windy weather.

examples.hanzi: 她涂了红色的口红，嘴唇很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Tā tú le hóngsè de kǒuhóng, zuǐchún hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: She put on red lipstick and her lips look pretty.

examples.hanzi: 天太冷了，他的嘴唇都冻紫了。
examples.pinyin: Tiān tài lěng le, tā de zuǐchún dōu dòng zǐ le.
examples.english: It was so cold that his lips turned purple.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐; oldest form shows a hand arranging a woman's hair, a wife.

example.hanzi: 他和妻子住在上海。
example.pinyin: Tā hé qīzi zhù zài Shànghǎi.
example.english: He lives in Shanghai with his wife.
example.fact: 妻 usually appears in 妻子 (wife) and 夫妻 (married couple), and is more formal than the colloquial 老婆. In compounds it is bound: you rarely say 妻 alone.

examples.hanzi: 他的妻子是一位医生。
examples.pinyin: Tā de qīzi shì yí wèi yīshēng.
examples.english: His wife is a doctor.

examples.hanzi: 这对夫妻结婚十年了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duì fūqī jiéhūn shí nián le.
examples.english: This couple has been married for ten years.

components.note: 矛 — a picture of a spear with its pointed head; in 矛盾 it pairs with 盾 shield: the old tale of the seller who boasted of both.
盾 (shield) — a shield held in front of the face; pairs with 矛 spear in 矛盾. 盾 dùn also sounds out 遁 dùn.

example.hanzi: 他的说法前后矛盾，让人难以相信。
example.pinyin: tā de shuōfǎ qiánhòu máodùn, ràng rén nányǐ xiāngxìn.
example.english: His statements contradicted each other, making it hard to believe him.
example.fact: In 1931, mathematician Kurt Gödel proved his incompleteness theorems, showing that any sufficiently powerful mathematical system contains true statements that can never be proven within that system. It was a landmark discovery about the built-in limits of logical consistency itself.

examples.hanzi: 他们之间有一些矛盾，需要沟通。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhījiān yǒu yìxiē máodùn, xūyào gōutōng.
examples.english: There are some conflicts between them that need communication.

examples.hanzi: 我的心情很矛盾，不知道该不该去。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xīnqíng hěn máodùn, bù zhīdào gāi bu gāi qù.
examples.english: I'm torn and don't know whether I should go.

components.note: 王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.
象 (elephant) — a picture of an elephant with trunk on top and legs below. 像 likeness adds 亻; 想象 imagine, 印象 impression use the "image" sense.

example.hanzi: 温室效应是一种全球性的气候现象。
example.pinyin: wēnshì xiàoyìng shì yī zhǒng quánqiúxìng de qìhòu xiànxiàng.
example.english: The greenhouse effect is a global climate phenomenon.
example.fact: Venus has an atmosphere that is 96 percent carbon dioxide, which drives a runaway greenhouse effect and raises its surface temperature to about 465 degrees Celsius, hot enough to melt lead. That makes Venus the hottest planet in the solar system, even though Mercury sits closer to the sun.

examples.hanzi: 这种现象在大城市里很常见。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng xiànxiàng zài dà chéngshì lǐ hěn chángjiàn.
examples.english: This phenomenon is very common in big cities.

examples.hanzi: 不要只看现象，要看本质。
examples.pinyin: Búyào zhǐ kàn xiànxiàng, yào kàn běnzhì.
examples.english: Don't just look at appearances; look at the essence.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.

example.hanzi: 这种药物结合了两种不同的治疗方式。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng yàowù jiéhé le liǎng zhǒng bùtóng de zhìliáo fāngshì.
example.english: This medicine combines two different treatment approaches.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin by accident in 1928 when mold contaminated a bacterial culture in his lab. Combined with mass-production techniques developed during World War II, it became the first widely used antibiotic, a pairing credited with saving hundreds of millions of lives since.

examples.hanzi: 学习要和实践结合起来。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxí yào hé shíjiàn jiéhé qǐlái.
examples.english: Study should be combined with practice.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅结合了中餐和西餐的特点。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng jiéhé le zhōngcān hé xīcān de tèdiǎn.
examples.english: This restaurant combines features of Chinese and Western cuisine.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: a strange feeling.
圣 here is not the "sage" word; it is only a loose sound clue for guài.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 邻居都觉得他是个怪人，很少和人说话。
example.pinyin: línjū dōu juéde tā shì gè guàirén, hěn shǎo hé rén shuōhuà.
example.english: The neighbors all think he's an eccentric, and he rarely talks to people.
example.fact: Nikola Tesla was famously eccentric, reportedly counting his steps obsessively and requiring exactly 18 napkins at every dinner. Despite these quirks, his work on alternating current still underlies most of the electrical grid used around the world today.

examples.hanzi: 他是个怪人，喜欢半夜出门散步。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè guàirén, xǐhuan bànyè chūmén sànbù.
examples.english: He's an oddball who likes taking walks in the middle of the night.

examples.hanzi: 别叫他怪人，他只是有点害羞。
examples.pinyin: Bié jiào tā guàirén, tā zhǐshì yǒudiǎn hàixiū.
examples.english: Don't call him a weirdo; he's just a bit shy.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 像 resemble; 似 is to look like.
以 (yǐ) is only a loose sound hint for sì.

example.hanzi: 这对姐妹的长相非常相似。
example.pinyin: zhè duì jiěmèi de zhǎngxiàng fēicháng xiāngsì.
example.english: The two sisters look very similar.
example.fact: Chimpanzees share about 98.8 percent of their DNA with humans, making them our closest living relatives. The similarity is close enough that some biologists have proposed reclassifying chimpanzees within the same genus as humans.

examples.hanzi: 这两个字的写法很相似。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè zì de xiěfǎ hěn xiāngsì.
examples.english: These two characters are written in a very similar way.

examples.hanzi: 我们的兴趣爱好非常相似。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de xìngqù àihào fēicháng xiāngsì.
examples.english: Our hobbies and interests are very similar.

components.note: 谷 — water (八) flowing out of a valley mouth (口). It also sounds out 浴 yù, 欲 yù and 俗 sú.

example.hanzi: 山谷里很安静。
example.pinyin: Shāngǔ lǐ hěn ānjìng.
example.english: The valley is very quiet.
example.fact: 谷 is 'valley' (山谷, 峡谷) and, in the simplified script, also 'grain', because 谷 replaced 穀 (谷物, grain crops). 硅谷 is Silicon Valley and 谷歌 is the transliteration of Google.

examples.hanzi: 秋天农民收割谷子。
examples.pinyin: Qiūtiān nóngmín shōugē gǔzi.
examples.english: Farmers harvest grain in autumn.

examples.hanzi: 硅谷有很多科技公司。
examples.pinyin: Guīgǔ yǒu hěn duō kējì gōngsī.
examples.english: Silicon Valley has many tech companies.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — hands throwing something out: 弃 is to cast away.

example.hanzi: 他不想放弃这个机会。
example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng fàngqì zhège jīhuì.
example.english: He doesn't want to give up this opportunity.
example.fact: 弃 is formal and mostly in compounds: 放弃 (to give up), 废弃 (abandon), 遗弃 (to desert) and 弃权 (to abstain from voting).

examples.hanzi: 不要随意丢弃垃圾。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào suíyì diūqì lājī.
examples.english: Don't throw rubbish away carelessly.

examples.hanzi: 这件旧家具已经被废弃了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn jiù jiājù yǐjīng bèi fèiqì le.
examples.english: This old furniture has already been discarded.

components.note: 后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).
田 (field) — the bottom part. 备 is simplified from 備; the dictionary story is a trip to the 田 field to prepare for harvest. Treat it as a memory aid.
夂 (going down, slow step) — the top. Memory aid: heading 夂 to the field 田 to get ready — 准备, 设备.

example.hanzi: 公司为电力中断准备了后备发电机。
example.pinyin: gōngsī wèi diànlì zhōngduàn zhǔnbèi le hòubèi fādiànjī.
example.english: The company prepared a backup generator in case of power outages.
example.fact: The International Space Station maintains multiple redundant backup systems for oxygen, water, and power, including several independent life-support pathways. Because no repair crew can reach the station quickly, engineers design every critical system with at least one backup in case the primary one fails.

examples.hanzi: 他是球队的后备队员，很少上场。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì qiúduì de hòubèi duìyuán, hěn shǎo shàngchǎng.
examples.english: He is a reserve player on the team and rarely gets on the field.

examples.hanzi: 出门的时候，我在后备箱里放了一把伞。
examples.pinyin: Chūmén de shíhou, wǒ zài hòubèixiāng lǐ fàng le yì bǎ sǎn.
examples.english: When heading out, I put an umbrella in the trunk.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球, 现, 理: 玩 first meant to handle jade.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 偶 first meant a figure or doll, then a pair.
禺 (yú) is a loose sound clue; same part in 遇 yù, 愚 yú, 寓 yù.

example.hanzi: 她的房间里摆满了各种玩偶。
example.pinyin: tā de fángjiān lǐ bǎi mǎn le gèzhǒng wánǒu.
example.english: Her room is filled with all kinds of dolls.
example.fact: Since Mattel launched the Barbie doll in 1959, it has sold more than a billion units worldwide and has been given over 200 different careers. The doll's shifting jobs over six decades have often been read as a mirror of changing ideas about women's roles in society.

examples.hanzi: 孩子抱着玩偶睡着了。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bàozhe wán'ǒu shuìzháo le.
examples.english: The child fell asleep hugging a stuffed toy.

examples.hanzi: 这个玩偶是我朋友送给我的生日礼物。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wán'ǒu shì wǒ péngyou sòng gěi wǒ de shēngrì lǐwù.
examples.english: This figurine was a birthday present from my friend.

components.note: 页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 颜; 领 is the neck and then to lead.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 领 is lǐng; 令 also sounds out 龄 líng and 铃 líng.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth and land, as in 地, 城; 域 is a territory.
或 (huò) — near sound — 域 is yù; 或 also sounds out 惑 huò.

example.hanzi: 人工智能是当今发展最快的科技领域之一。
example.pinyin: réngōng zhìnéng shì dāngjīn fāzhǎn zuì kuài de kējì lǐngyù zhī yī.
example.english: Artificial intelligence is one of the fastest-developing fields in technology today.
example.fact: The term 'artificial intelligence' was coined in 1956 at the Dartmouth Summer Research Project, a workshop attended by fewer than 20 researchers. They optimistically believed a machine could be built to reason like a human within a single summer, a goal that took many more decades to even partially realize.

examples.hanzi: 他在医学领域有很高的成就。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yīxué lǐngyù yǒu hěn gāo de chéngjiù.
examples.english: He has made great achievements in the field of medicine.

examples.hanzi: 这不是我熟悉的领域，我帮不了你。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bú shì wǒ shúxī de lǐngyù, wǒ bāng bù liǎo nǐ.
examples.english: This isn't a field I'm familiar with, so I can't help you.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.
纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and ties, as in 线, 红, 约; 缘 first meant a hem, then the tie of fate.
彖 (tuàn) is only a loose hint for yuán.

example.hanzi: 那只鹿站在森林的边缘警觉地望着四周。
example.pinyin: nà zhī lù zhàn zài sēnlín de biānyuán jǐngjué de wàng zhe sìzhōu.
example.english: The deer stood at the edge of the forest, watching its surroundings alertly.
example.fact: Ecologists have found that the outer edges of tropical rainforests lose moisture and biodiversity faster than the interior, because sun and wind exposure can dry out soil up to a kilometer inward. This 'edge effect' is a major concern in the Amazon, where deforestation keeps fragmenting the forest into more and more exposed edges.

examples.hanzi: 别站在悬崖的边缘，太危险了。
examples.pinyin: Bié zhàn zài xuányá de biānyuán, tài wēixiǎn le.
examples.english: Don't stand at the edge of the cliff; it's too dangerous.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司已经处在破产的边缘。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yǐjīng chǔ zài pòchǎn de biānyuán.
examples.english: This company is already on the verge of bankruptcy.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 骑自行车时一定要戴头部保护装置。
example.pinyin: qí zìxíngchē shí yīdìng yào dài tóubù bǎohù zhuāngzhì.
example.english: You must wear head protection when riding a bicycle.
example.fact: The human head makes up only about 8 percent of total body weight, but the brain inside it consumes roughly 20 percent of the body's resting energy. No other organ uses anywhere near that share of the body's fuel relative to its size.

examples.hanzi: 他的头部受了点轻伤。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tóubù shòu le diǎn qīngshāng.
examples.english: He had a slight injury to his head.

examples.hanzi: 这种鸟的头部是红色的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng niǎo de tóubù shì hóngsè de.
examples.english: This kind of bird has a red head.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤: clear water.
青 (qīng) gives the exact sound; also 请 qǐng, 情 qíng, 晴 qíng and 精 jīng.
单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.

example.hanzi: 出发前她检查了一遍行李清单。
example.pinyin: chūfā qián tā jiǎnchá le yī biàn xínglǐ qīngdān.
example.english: Before departure, she went through her packing checklist once.
example.fact: Surgeon Atul Gawande helped popularize the surgical safety checklist after a 2009 WHO-backed study across eight hospitals worldwide. Simply requiring teams to confirm a short list of basic steps before operating cut major surgical complications by more than a third.

examples.hanzi: 我列了一张购物清单。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ liè le yì zhāng gòuwù qīngdān.
examples.english: I made a shopping list.

examples.hanzi: 这是今年的愿望清单。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì jīnnián de yuànwàng qīngdān.
examples.english: This is this year's wish list.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 振 is to shake or rouse.
辰 (chén) hints at the sound: 振 zhèn is close to 震 zhèn, which shares it.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.hanzi: 经历失败后，他很快振作起来重新开始训练。
example.pinyin: jīnglì shībài hòu, tā hěn kuài zhènzuò qǐlái chóngxīn kāishǐ xùnliàn.
example.english: After the failure, he quickly pulled himself together and resumed training.
example.fact: Michael Jordan was cut from his high school varsity basketball team as a sophomore. He later said the setback fueled the relentless training habits that helped him become one of the greatest players in NBA history.

examples.hanzi: 你要振作起来，不要太难过。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào zhènzuò qǐlái, búyào tài nánguò.
examples.english: Pull yourself together; don't be too sad.

examples.hanzi: 听到好消息，大家的精神都振作了。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào hǎo xiāoxi, dàjiā de jīngshén dōu zhènzuò le.
examples.english: Hearing the good news lifted everyone's spirits.

components.note: 亠 (lid) — the top part, a cap. Memory aid: a lid on top of 允 suggests something filled up to the lid, hence 'fill, be full' as in 充满.
允 (yǔn, permit) — the bottom part; it is a visible piece, but not a sound clue today (充 is chōng). Memory aid: allowed to fill up.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.hanzi: 做这个决定之前，我们需要充分的证据。
example.pinyin: zuò zhège juédìng zhīqián, wǒmen xūyào chōngfèn de zhèngjù.
example.english: Before making this decision, we need sufficient evidence.
example.fact: The Royal Society's Philosophical Transactions, launched in 1665, is considered the first scientific journal to systematically require sufficient supporting evidence before publishing a claim. That review process eventually grew into the peer-review system scientific journals still use today.

examples.hanzi: 考试前一定要充分休息。
examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì qián yídìng yào chōngfèn xiūxi.
examples.english: Be sure to get plenty of rest before the exam.

examples.hanzi: 我们要充分利用这段时间。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào chōngfèn lìyòng zhè duàn shíjiān.
examples.english: We should make full use of this time.

meanings: (lit. and fig.) to come back to life

components.note: 复 (fù) sounds out 腹 fù belly and 覆 fù cover; as a word it means again or to repeat, as in 恢复, 重复.
氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤; water means life: 活 is alive.
舌 (shé, tongue) is a loose sound clue for huó; also in 话 huà.

example.hanzi: 科学家试图利用基因技术复活已灭绝的物种。
example.pinyin: kēxuéjiā shìtú lìyòng jīyīn jìshù fùhuó yǐ mièjué de wùzhǒng.
example.english: Scientists are trying to use genetic technology to revive extinct species.
example.fact: In 2023, researchers successfully extracted RNA from a 130-year-old preserved Tasmanian tiger specimen, the first time RNA had ever been recovered from an extinct species. Some scientists hope such molecules could eventually support 'de-extinction' efforts, though a living Tasmanian tiger remains far off.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲的是一个人死后复活的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng de shì yí gè rén sǐ hòu fùhuó de gùshi.
examples.english: This movie tells a story of a person who comes back to life after death.

examples.hanzi: 春天来了，枯萎的草又复活了。
examples.pinyin: Chūntiān lái le, kūwěi de cǎo yòu fùhuó le.
examples.english: Spring has come, and the withered grass has revived.

components.note: 又 (hand) — 双 (simplified 雙) shows two birds held in one hand: a pair; the simplified form just doubles the hand 又又.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 胞 is the womb, then a cell (细胞).
包 (bāo) gives the sound exactly: 胞 bāo, also in 饱 bǎo and 抱 bào.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 胎 is a fetus, and by extension a tyre.
台 (tái) gives the sound exactly: 胎 tāi is close.

example.hanzi: 这对双胞胎从小就形影不离。
example.pinyin: zhè duì shuāngbāotāi cóngxiǎo jiù xíngyǐngbùlí.
example.english: These twins have been inseparable since childhood.
example.fact: Identical twins form when a single fertilized egg splits into two embryos, giving them nearly identical DNA. Even so, their fingerprints still differ, because ridge patterns are shaped partly by random pressure and position inside the womb rather than genetics alone.

examples.hanzi: 她生了一对双胞胎，一个男孩一个女孩。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēng le yí duì shuāngbāotāi, yí gè nánhái yí gè nǚhái.
examples.english: She gave birth to twins, a boy and a girl.

examples.hanzi: 你们是双胞胎吗？长得真像！
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen shì shuāngbāotāi ma? Zhǎng de zhēn xiàng!
examples.english: Are you twins? You look so alike!

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and ranks, as in 院, 阶, 防; 阵 is a battle formation.
车 (chariot) — war chariots lined up in rows.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 他们在公园里聊了一阵子才离开。
example.pinyin: tāmen zài gōngyuán lǐ liáo le yī zhènzi cái líkāi.
example.english: They chatted in the park for a while before leaving.
example.fact: A 'jiffy' is an informal but sometimes formally used unit of time, defined in physics as roughly 33.4 picoseconds — the time light takes to travel one centimeter — while in early computing it instead meant about 1/100th of a second, depending on the field using it.

examples.hanzi: 这一阵子我特别忙，没时间见你。
examples.pinyin: Zhè yízhènzi wǒ tèbié máng, méi shíjiān jiàn nǐ.
examples.english: I've been especially busy these days and had no time to see you.

examples.hanzi: 他愣了一阵子，才反应过来。
examples.pinyin: Tā lèng le yízhènzi, cái fǎnyìng guòlái.
examples.english: He was stunned for a moment before he reacted.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speaking and asking, as in 吗, 呢, 问: 哪 is a question word.
那 (nà) gives the same syllable in a different tone; compare 那 "that" and 哪 "which".
此 (cǐ) is a loose sound clue for xiē; 此 also sounds out 紫 zǐ and 雌 cí. 些 is the plural-ish "some, a few".

example.hanzi: 你知道哪些国家使用人民币作为官方货币吗？
example.pinyin: nǐ zhīdào nǎxiē guójiā shǐyòng rénmínbì zuòwéi guānfāng huòbì ma?
example.english: Do you know which countries use the renminbi as their official currency?
example.fact: The US dollar is the official or de facto currency in more than a dozen countries outside the United States, including Ecuador, El Salvador, and Zimbabwe. Each of these countries 'dollarized' its economy after a period of severe hyperinflation made its own currency unusable.

examples.hanzi: 你想去哪些城市旅游？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng qù nǎxiē chéngshì lǚyóu?
examples.english: Which cities do you want to visit?

examples.hanzi: 这些书里，哪些是你的？
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shū lǐ, nǎxiē shì nǐ de?
examples.english: Of these books, which ones are yours?

components.note: 冫 (ice) — here the ice form of 氵 (water): 决 first meant to break a dam, so a decisive break.
夬 (guài) is a loose sound clue for jué; 夬 also sounds out 快 kuài and 块 kuài.

example.hanzi: 我决定明天去北京。
example.pinyin: Wǒ juédìng míngtiān qù Běijīng.
example.english: I decided to go to Beijing tomorrow.
example.fact: 决 once meant to break open a dam (决堤), and from the idea of 'cutting a clear path' it came to mean 'decide': 决定, 决心 (determination) and 决赛 (finals). 决 also means 'definitely' in 决不 'absolutely not'.

examples.hanzi: 这件事要尽快解决。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yào jǐnkuài jiějué.
examples.english: This matter needs to be resolved as soon as possible.

examples.hanzi: 他很坚决,不会改变主意。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn jiānjué, bú huì gǎibiàn zhǔyi.
examples.english: He is firm and won't change his mind.

components.note: 彡 (decorative strokes) — marks patterns and adornment, as in 形 shape, 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 修 is to tidy and decorate, then repair.
攸 (yōu) is only a loose hint for xiū; 悠 yōu shares it.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 师傅正在修理那台坏掉的洗衣机。
example.pinyin: shīfu zhèngzài xiūlǐ nà tái huàidiào de xǐyījī.
example.english: The technician is repairing that broken washing machine.
example.fact: Shortly after the Hubble Space Telescope launched in 1990, engineers discovered a flaw in its main mirror that blurred its images. A 1993 space shuttle repair mission installed corrective optics, fixing Hubble's vision and enabling it to later capture famous images like the 'Pillars of Creation.'

examples.hanzi: 我的手机屏幕碎了，要去修理。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī píngmù suì le, yào qù xiūlǐ.
examples.english: My phone screen is broken and needs repairing.

examples.hanzi: 哥哥会修理自行车和电脑。
examples.pinyin: Gēge huì xiūlǐ zìxíngchē hé diànnǎo.
examples.english: My older brother can fix bikes and computers.

components.note: 肖 (xiāo) — to resemble; as a part it sounds out 消 xiāo, 销 xiāo, 宵 xiāo and 俏 qiào.
心 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 想, 爱, 思; 恩 is kindness, gratitude of the heart.
因 (yīn) is only a loose sound hint for ēn.

example.hanzi: 肖恩每天早上都去公园跑步。
example.pinyin: Xiāo ēn měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
example.english: Sean goes jogging in the park every morning.
example.fact: The name 'Sean' is the Anglicized spelling of the Irish 'Seán,' which itself descends from the Hebrew name 'John' by way of the French 'Jean.' The chain reflects centuries of contact between Irish, French, and Biblical naming traditions.

examples.hanzi: 肖恩是我们公司的新同事。
examples.pinyin: Xiāo'ēn shì wǒmen gōngsī de xīn tóngshì.
examples.english: Sean is a new colleague at our company.

examples.hanzi: 肖恩和他的朋友在咖啡馆见面。
examples.pinyin: Xiāo'ēn hé tā de péngyou zài kāfēiguǎn jiànmiàn.
examples.english: Sean and his friend are meeting at a café.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — the bottom part, as in 布, 帽, 带. 希 is often read as a loosely woven cloth, so 'sparse, rare'; 希望 hope is a later extension.
乂 (crisscross) — Memory aid: crossed threads in an open weave 乂 on cloth 巾 — thin, rare, something you hope for.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
革 (leather) — marks hides and straps, as in 鞋, 靴 boots, 鞭 whip; 勒 is to rein in or tighten.
力 (lì) is only a loose sound hint for lè.

example.hanzi: 历史课上老师讲述了希特勒发动战争的历史背景。
example.pinyin: lìshǐ kè shàng lǎoshī jiǎngshù le Xītèlè fādòng zhànzhēng de lìshǐ bèijǐng.
example.english: In history class, the teacher explained the historical background of Hitler starting the war.
example.fact: Adolf Hitler applied to Vienna's Academy of Fine Arts twice as a young man and was rejected both times before turning to politics. Historians still cite this documented failure when speculating about how differently the 20th century might have unfolded.

examples.hanzi: 我们在历史课上学了希特勒上台的经过。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài lìshǐ kè shàng xué le Xītèlè shàngtái de jīngguò.
examples.english: In history class we studied how Hitler came to power.

examples.hanzi: 这本书分析了希特勒的宣传手段。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū fēnxī le Xītèlè de xuānchuán shǒuduàn.
examples.english: This book analyzes Hitler's propaganda methods.

components.note: 夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: a building holds things.
谷 (valley) — a hollow that holds: 容 is to hold or allow.

example.hanzi: 她脸上一直挂着温暖的笑容。
example.pinyin: tā liǎn shàng yīzhí guà zhe wēnnuǎn de xiàoróng.
example.english: She always had a warm smile on her face.
example.fact: Genuine smiles, known to researchers as Duchenne smiles, engage both the mouth muscles and the orbicularis oculi muscles around the eyes. Studies show people can usually tell a genuine smile from a posed one within a fraction of a second, even from a photograph.

examples.hanzi: 孩子的笑容让大家都很开心。
examples.pinyin: Háizi de xiàoróng ràng dàjiā dōu hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: The child's smile made everyone happy.

examples.hanzi: 服务员脸上带着亲切的笑容。
examples.pinyin: Fúwùyuán liǎn shàng dàizhe qīnqiè de xiàoróng.
examples.english: The waiter wore a friendly smile.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: to grip or rely on.
居 (jū) is a close sound clue for jù; 居 also in 剧 jù and 锯 jù.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.hanzi: 据说这座古庙已经有上千年的历史了。
example.pinyin: jùshuō zhè zuò gǔmiào yǐjīng yǒu shàng qiān nián de lìshǐ le.
example.english: It is said that this ancient temple has a history of over a thousand years.
example.fact: Angkor Wat in Cambodia, often called the largest religious monument in the world, was originally built as a Hindu temple in the early 12th century. Over the following centuries it gradually transformed into a Buddhist site, a shift still visible in its carvings today.

examples.hanzi: 据说明天会下大雪。
examples.pinyin: Jùshuō míngtiān huì xià dàxuě.
examples.english: It is said that it will snow heavily tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的面条据说是全城最好吃的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de miàntiáo jùshuō shì quán chéng zuì hǎochī de.
examples.english: The noodles at this shop are said to be the best in the city.

components.note: 电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).
氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 湖; 池 is a pond.
也 (yě) hints at the sound: 池 chí is close to 驰 chí and 弛 chí.

example.hanzi: 手机的电池只剩下百分之十的电量。
example.pinyin: shǒujī de diànchí zhǐ shèng xià bǎi fēn zhī shí de diànliàng.
example.english: The phone's battery only has 10 percent power left.
example.fact: Sony commercialized the first lithium-ion battery in 1991, and the technology now powers nearly every smartphone and electric vehicle. Its inventors, John Goodenough, M. Stanley Whittingham, and Akira Yoshino, shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing it.

examples.hanzi: 遥控器没电了，要换电池。
examples.pinyin: Yáokòngqì méi diàn le, yào huàn diànchí.
examples.english: The remote is out of power and needs new batteries.

examples.hanzi: 这款笔记本的电池可以用十个小时。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn bǐjìběn de diànchí kěyǐ yòng shí gè xiǎoshí.
examples.english: This laptop's battery lasts ten hours.

components.note: 尸 (a sitting person, body) — a figure at rest or a building: 屋 house, 层 floor, 尾 tail; 居 is to dwell.
古 (gǔ) is a loose clue; 居 jū sounds out 据 jù, 剧 jù and 锯 jù.
民 (people) — one old theory sees an eye pierced by a pointed tool, a mark of those with no rights; the meaning "ordinary people" is what to remember.

example.hanzi: 当地居民对新建的工厂表示强烈反对。
example.pinyin: dāngdì jūmín duì xīnjiàn de gōngchǎng biǎoshì qiángliè fǎnduì.
example.english: Local residents strongly opposed the newly built factory.
example.fact: Greater Tokyo is home to roughly 37 million residents, making it the most populous urban area on Earth. That single metropolitan area holds more people than the entire population of Canada.

examples.hanzi: 小区的居民要求增加停车位。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoqū de jūmín yāoqiú zēngjiā tíngchēwèi.
examples.english: Residents of the neighborhood asked for more parking spaces.

examples.hanzi: 这座小城只有五千名居民。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò xiǎo chéng zhǐ yǒu wǔ qiān míng jūmín.
examples.english: This small town has only five thousand inhabitants.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical (单人旁) — 价 is about what people pay or the worth of things; also in 你, 他, 住.
介 (jiè) — near-sound hint — 价 is jià; 介 also sounds out 界 jiè and 阶 jiē.

example.hanzi: 这个东西的价格太高了。
example.pinyin: Zhège dōngxi de jiàgé tài gāo le.
example.english: The price of this thing is too high.
example.fact: Simplified 价 replaces 價 and is read jià: 价格 (price), 价钱 (price), 价值 (value), 降价 (cut prices). The older 价 read jiè, with a different meaning, is rare and not what you see today.

examples.hanzi: 这本书的定价是五十元。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de dìngjià shì wǔshí yuán.
examples.english: This book is priced at fifty yuan.

examples.hanzi: 这个手机性价比很高。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒujī xìngjiàbǐ hěn gāo.
examples.english: This phone is great value for money.

components.note: 厂 (shelter) — 厂 here stands for a building; the traditional 廳 had 广, a wide hall.
丁 (dīng) — near sound — 厅 is tīng; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng and 顶 dǐng.

example.hanzi: 客厅里有一张大沙发。
example.pinyin: Kètīng lǐ yǒu yì zhāng dà shāfā.
example.english: There is a big sofa in the living room.
example.fact: 厅 is a hall: 客厅 (living room), 餐厅 (restaurant, dining room) and 大厅 (lobby). It also names provincial government departments like 教育厅.

examples.hanzi: 我们在餐厅见面吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài cāntīng jiànmiàn ba.
examples.english: Let's meet at the restaurant.

examples.hanzi: 大厅里有很多人在等候。
examples.pinyin: Dàtīng li yǒu hěn duō rén zài děnghòu.
examples.english: Many people are waiting in the hall.

components.note: 平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.

example.hanzi: 家人只希望他能平安回家。
example.pinyin: jiārén zhǐ xīwàng tā néng píng'ān huí jiā.
example.english: His family only hoped he could return home safe and sound.
example.fact: The 'black box' flight recorders carried on commercial aircraft are actually painted bright orange, not black. The color is chosen specifically so rescue teams can spot the device quickly among wreckage after a crash.

examples.hanzi: 到了以后给我打个电话，报个平安。
examples.pinyin: Dào le yǐhòu gěi wǒ dǎ gè diànhuà, bào gè píng'ān.
examples.english: Call me when you arrive to let me know you're safe.

examples.hanzi: 祝你们一路平安！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐmen yílù píng'ān!
examples.english: Wishing you a safe journey!

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 拿, 提, 抬; 搬 is to move things.
般 (bān) gives the sound exactly: 搬 bān.
走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.

example.hanzi: 他们上个月把所有家具都搬走了。
example.pinyin: tāmen shàng gè yuè bǎ suǒyǒu jiājù dōu bān zǒu le.
example.english: They moved all the furniture away last month.
example.fact: In 1999, engineers moved the entire 4,800-ton Cape Hatteras Lighthouse nearly 2,900 feet inland on steel rails and rollers to save it from coastal erosion. It remains one of the largest brick structure relocations ever carried out.

examples.hanzi: 请把这些纸箱搬走。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhèxiē zhǐxiāng bānzǒu.
examples.english: Please carry these cardboard boxes away.

examples.hanzi: 我的邻居上个星期搬走了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de línjū shàng gè xīngqī bānzǒu le.
examples.english: My neighbor moved out last week.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — marks insects, as in 蜂 bee, 蚊, 蜘; wax comes from bees, hence 蜡.
昔 (xī) is a loose hint for là; 腊 là shares it.
火 (fire) — marks fire and light, as in 灯, 烧, 燃; 烛 is a candle. The 虫 stands in for an old part 蜀 (shǔ) that gave the sound.

example.hanzi: 生日蛋糕上插满了蜡烛。
example.pinyin: shēngrì dàngāo shàng chā mǎn le làzhú.
example.english: The birthday cake was covered with candles.
example.fact: Before electric lighting, candles were commonly made from tallow (animal fat) or beeswax. Beeswax candles burned much cleaner and longer than tallow ones, which made them a costly luxury reserved mostly for churches and wealthy households in medieval Europe.

examples.hanzi: 停电了，我们点了一根蜡烛。
examples.pinyin: Tíngdiàn le, wǒmen diǎn le yì gēn làzhú.
examples.english: The power went out, so we lit a candle.

examples.hanzi: 晚餐的时候，桌上摆着浪漫的蜡烛。
examples.pinyin: Wǎncān de shíhou, zhuō shàng bǎizhe làngmàn de làzhú.
examples.english: During dinner, romantic candles were on the table.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.
亠 (lid) — the top stroke group, as in 市 and 交. The sound-borrowed number; no meaning link. Memory aid: a lid on top of 八 (eight) ends up as six.
八 (eight) — the bottom part, as in 分 divide. Same shape as 'eight' but the number 六 does not come from it; use it as a visual memory aid.

example.hanzi: 我们星期六约好一起去爬山。
example.pinyin: wǒmen Xīngqīliù yuē hǎo yīqǐ qù páshān.
example.english: We agreed to go hiking together on Saturday.
example.fact: Saturday is the only day of the week in English named directly after a Roman deity, Saturn, while most other English weekday names come from Norse gods instead. The mismatch is a linguistic leftover from Roman astrology blending with later Germanic naming traditions.

examples.hanzi: 星期六我通常睡到中午才起床。
examples.pinyin: Xīngqīliù wǒ tōngcháng shuì dào zhōngwǔ cái qǐchuáng.
examples.english: On Saturdays I usually sleep until noon.

examples.hanzi: 这个星期六你有空吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhège xīngqīliù nǐ yǒu kòng ma?
examples.english: Are you free this Saturday?

components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 生病的时候，最想见到的就是亲人。
example.pinyin: shēngbìng de shíhòu, zuì xiǎng jiàndào de jiùshì qīnrén.
example.english: When you're sick, the people you most want to see are your close relatives.
example.fact: Researchers studying elephant social bonds have found that they maintain lifelong relationships with close relatives. Grieving elephants have even been observed returning repeatedly to the bones of deceased family members, touching and investigating the remains for years afterward.

examples.hanzi: 过年的时候，亲人们都会聚在一起。
examples.pinyin: Guònián de shíhou, qīnrénmen dōu huì jù zài yìqǐ.
examples.english: During the New Year, relatives all get together.

examples.hanzi: 他在这个城市没有亲人。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhège chéngshì méiyǒu qīnrén.
examples.english: He has no family in this city.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
幺 (small/thread) — the dictionary radical, as in 么 and 幻. 乡 is simplified from 鄉 (village); the three strokes here look like a thread. Memory aid: a thread looping home to the village.

example.hanzi: 每年春节，他都会回家乡看望父母。
example.pinyin: měinián chūnjié, tā dōu huì huí jiāxiāng kànwàng fùmǔ.
example.english: Every Spring Festival, he returns to his hometown to visit his parents.
example.fact: China's Spring Festival travel rush, known as chunyun, is the largest annual human migration on Earth, with billions of trips made in about 40 days. Most of that movement is people returning to their hometowns for the holiday before heading back to work afterward.

examples.hanzi: 我很想念家乡的美食。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xiǎngniàn jiāxiāng de měishí.
examples.english: I really miss the food of my hometown.

examples.hanzi: 他的家乡是一个安静的小山村。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jiāxiāng shì yí gè ānjìng de xiǎo shāncūn.
examples.english: His hometown is a quiet little mountain village.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
上 (above) — 上 over 下 squeezed together: something stuck in the middle, the sense of qiǎ (to wedge); kǎ is the borrowed sound for "card" and "car", as in 信用卡 and 卡车.
囗 (enclosure) — here a mat; oldest form shows a person 大 lying on a mat, "to rely on", later "cause". 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn and 烟 yān.

example.hanzi: 警方在仓库里查获了大量可卡因。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng zài cāngkù lǐ cháhuò le dàliàng kěkǎyīn.
example.english: Police seized a large quantity of cocaine in the warehouse.
example.fact: Cocaine comes from the leaves of the coca plant native to the Andes, which indigenous peoples there have chewed for thousands of years to fight altitude sickness and fatigue at high elevation. The active alkaloid itself was not chemically isolated until 1860.

examples.hanzi: 可卡因是一种危险的毒品。
examples.pinyin: Kěkǎyīn shì yì zhǒng wēixiǎn de dúpǐn.
examples.english: Cocaine is a dangerous drug.

examples.hanzi: 海关在行李里发现了可卡因。
examples.pinyin: Hǎiguān zài xínglǐ lǐ fāxiàn le kěkǎyīn.
examples.english: Customs found cocaine in the luggage.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and speed, as in 过, 进, 送; 迅 is rapid.
卂 (xùn) gives the sound exactly: 迅 xùn, also in 讯 xùn.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving — 速 is speed, as in 快速 and 速度.
束 (shù) — near sound — 速 is sù, same syllable with different initial.

example.hanzi: 消防员迅速赶到现场展开救援。
example.pinyin: xiāofángyuán xùnsù gǎndào xiànchǎng zhǎnkāi jiùyuán.
example.english: The firefighters rapidly arrived at the scene to begin the rescue.
example.fact: Peregrine falcons can exceed 320 kilometers per hour during a hunting dive, making them the fastest animals on Earth by a wide margin. Specialized bony structures in their nostrils let them keep breathing safely despite the extreme airflow at that speed.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市的经济发展得很迅速。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì de jīngjì fāzhǎn de hěn xùnsù.
examples.english: This city's economy is developing rapidly.

examples.hanzi: 他迅速地回答了老师的问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā xùnsù de huídá le lǎoshī de wèntí.
examples.english: He quickly answered the teacher's question.

components.note: 米 (rice) — refined grain gives the idea of essence and the best part, hence 精 fine, spirit (精神).
青 (qīng) is a near sound match (-ing); the series 青 清 请 情 晴 静 helps recall jīng.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.
疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.

example.hanzi: 这项研究揭示了压力与精神病之间的关系。
example.pinyin: zhè xiàng yánjiū jiēshì le yālì yǔ jīngshénbìng zhījiān de guānxì.
example.english: This study reveals the relationship between stress and mental illness.
example.fact: The World Health Organization estimates that roughly one in eight people worldwide lives with a mental disorder, and depression alone is among the leading causes of disability globally. Yet mental health typically receives less than 2 percent of average government health budgets.

examples.hanzi: 他被诊断患有精神病，需要长期治疗。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi zhěnduàn huànyǒu jīngshénbìng, xūyào chángqī zhìliáo.
examples.english: He was diagnosed with a mental disorder and needs long-term treatment.

examples.hanzi: 社会上不应该歧视精神病患者。
examples.pinyin: Shèhuì shàng bù yīnggāi qíshì jīngshénbìng huànzhě.
examples.english: Society shouldn't discriminate against people with mental illness.

components.note: 木 (wood) — marks trees and wooden things, as in 树, 桥, 板; 棺 is a wooden coffin.
官 (guān) gives the sound exactly: 棺 guān, also in 馆 guǎn and 管 guǎn.
木 (wood) — marks trees and timber, as in 树, 桥, 板; 材 is timber, then material.
才 (cái) gives the sound exactly: 材 cái, also in 财 cái.

example.hanzi: 工人们小心地把棺材抬进墓地。
example.pinyin: gōngrénmen xiǎoxīn de bǎ guāncai tái jìn mùdì.
example.english: The workers carefully carried the coffin into the cemetery.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptian pharaohs were often buried in nested sets of coffins, sometimes three or more, one placed inside another. Tutankhamun's innermost coffin was made of solid gold and weighed about 110 kilograms.

examples.hanzi: 棺材被缓缓放进了墓穴。
examples.pinyin: Guāncai bèi huǎnhuǎn fàng jìn le mùxué.
examples.english: The coffin was slowly lowered into the grave.

examples.hanzi: 这部恐怖片里有一口神秘的棺材。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù kǒngbùpiàn lǐ yǒu yì kǒu shénmì de guāncai.
examples.english: This horror film features a mysterious coffin.

components.note: 页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 颜; 领 is the neck and then to lead.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 领 is lǐng; 令 also sounds out 龄 líng and 铃 líng.
巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 帽, 帮: a belt of cloth with pieces hanging from it.

example.hanzi: 他每天上班都会打一条整齐的领带。
example.pinyin: tā měitiān shàngbān dōu huì dǎ yī tiáo zhěngqí de lǐngdài.
example.english: He wears a neatly tied necktie to work every day.
example.fact: The modern necktie is often traced to Croatian mercenaries serving in the French army in the 1660s, whose knotted neck scarves caught the eye of French nobility. Over the following centuries that accessory evolved through several styles into the necktie worn today.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸生日，我送了他一条蓝色领带。
examples.pinyin: Bàba shēngrì, wǒ sòng le tā yì tiáo lánsè lǐngdài.
examples.english: For Dad's birthday I gave him a blue tie.

examples.hanzi: 面试的时候要打领带吗？
examples.pinyin: Miànshì de shíhou yào dǎ lǐngdài ma?
examples.english: Do I need to wear a tie to the interview?

components.note: 牛 (ox) — a picture of an ox's head with horns; as a radical it marks cattle, in 牺, 牲, 牧, 物.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — arranging and moving by hand: 打, 推, 拉; 排 is to line things up.
非 (fēi) is a loose sound hint; its series includes 悲 bēi and 菲 fēi.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的牛排非常鲜嫩多汁。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā cāntīng de niúpái fēicháng xiānnèn duōzhī.
example.english: The steak at this restaurant is very tender and juicy.
example.fact: Wagyu cattle, prized for their intensely marbled beef, are raised in Japan under strict genetic lineage tracking. Each animal's pedigree can be traced back through registered records much like a racehorse's, which helps preserve the breed's distinctive marbling.

examples.hanzi: 你的牛排要几分熟？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de niúpái yào jǐ fēn shú?
examples.english: How would you like your steak cooked?

examples.hanzi: 周末我们去吃了一顿牛排大餐。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù chī le yí dùn niúpái dàcān.
examples.english: At the weekend we went for a big steak dinner.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.
彡 (patterns, hairlines) — marks shape, shadow and decoration, as in 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 形 is a shape.
开 (a worn-down 幵) hints at the sound: 形 xíng sounds like 刑 and 型.

example.hanzi: 医生详细说明了病人目前的情形。
example.pinyin: yīshēng xiángxì shuōmíng le bìngrén mùqián de qíngxing.
example.english: The doctor explained the patient's current situation in detail.
example.fact: Triage, the practice of assessing patients to decide who is treated first, originated on Napoleonic battlefields in the early 1800s. French military surgeon Dominique Jean Larrey developed the system to make sure the most urgent casualties were treated before less severe ones.

examples.hanzi: 这种情形下，我们只能等待。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng qíngxíng xià, wǒmen zhǐ néng děngdài.
examples.english: In this situation, all we can do is wait.

examples.hanzi: 请你描述一下当时的情形。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ miáoshù yíxià dāngshí de qíngxíng.
examples.english: Please describe what the situation was like at the time.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — the sheep family: 美, 养, 群. Dictionary story: work 工 done by a sheep — memory aid for being poor or off. Origin uncertain.
工 (work) — the bottom. Memory aid: poor work 工, so 差劲 poor quality. 差 is chā/chà (difference, lacking) or chāi (send).
力 (strength) — 力 is strength, as in 办, 动, 努; 劲 is energy and force.
又 (hand) — 又 here stands in for the older 巠, which gave the near sound: 经 jīng, 轻 qīng.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的特效真是差劲。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng de tèxiào zhēnshi chàjìn.
example.english: The special effects in this movie are really disappointing.
example.fact: The 1980 film 'Heaven's Gate' was such a critically panned, costly box-office failure that it lost the equivalent of roughly 100 million of today's dollars. Its collapse is often cited by film historians as a major cause of the fall of United Artists studio.

examples.hanzi: 他的服务态度真差劲。
examples.pinyin: Tā de fúwù tàidu zhēn chàjìn.
examples.english: His service attitude is really poor.

examples.hanzi: 我今天打球打得太差劲了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān dǎqiú dǎ de tài chàjìn le.
examples.english: I played terribly today.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
辶 (movement) — marks roads and travel, as in 过, 进, 送; 途 is a road or route.
余 (yú) is a loose hint for tú; 涂 tú shares it.

example.hanzi: 老师说他很有前途，应该继续深造。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī shuō tā hěn yǒu qiántú, yīnggāi jìxù shēnzào.
example.english: The teacher said he has great prospects and should continue his studies.
example.fact: Albert Einstein struggled to find an academic position after graduating and worked for several years as a patent clerk in Switzerland. That unpromising start came before he published his theory of special relativity in 1905, at the age of 26.

examples.hanzi: 这个行业很有前途。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hángyè hěn yǒu qiántú.
examples.english: This industry has a bright future.

examples.hanzi: 他放弃了稳定的工作，不顾前途。
examples.pinyin: Tā fàngqì le wěndìng de gōngzuò, bú gù qiántú.
examples.english: He gave up a stable job without regard for his prospects.
